chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Ibn Muskan, from Ibn Abi Yafur, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man: Does anything that passes in front of him cut off his prayer? He (peace be upon him) said: Nothing cuts off the prayer of the believer, but ward off (the passerby) as much as you can.

And in a narration of Ibn Muskan from Abu Baseer from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said: Nothing cuts off the prayer, neither a dog, nor a donkey, nor a woman, but cover yourself with something. So if there is in front of you a measurement of a cubit raised from the ground, then you have covered yourself.

Al-Kulayni and Al-Fazl said regarding this: You should cover yourself with something and place in front of you what you use to protect yourself from the passerby. If you do not do so, there is no harm in it, because the one for whom the pray-er is praying is closer to him than the one who passes in front of him, but that is the etiquette of the prayer and its reverence.
ai.seo_question: Does something passing in front of a person invalidate their prayer in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith clarifies the distinction between the validity (sahha) and perfection (kamal) of prayer, asserting that while a passerby does not invalidate the prayer, ignoring the sutrah neglects the etiquette (adab) and reverence (tawqir) of the prayer. The commentary by Al-Kulayni and Al-Fadl underscores that the Imam’s intercession is closer to the worshiper than the passerby, making the barrier a means of focusing devotion rather than a strict condition for validity. This reflects the Shia juristic principle of distinguishing between obligatory precautions and recommended adornments of worship.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Usman Bin Isa, from Ibn Muskan, from Ibn Abu Yafour who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about the man, ‘Should he cut off his Salāt due to anything from what passes by in front of him?’ So heasws said: ‘Nothing cuts off the Salāt of the Believer, but be protective, whatever you are able to’.

And in a report of Ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘Nothing cut off the Salāt, neither a dog, nor a donkey, nor a woman, but veil yourself with something. So if there was in front of you (something of) a measurement of a cubit raised from the ground (in height), so you would have veiled’.

Al-Kulayni and Al-Fazl said with regards to this, ‘You should veil with something and place it in front of you what you can protect with from the passer by. But if you do not do so, there is no problem with it, because the one who is praying is closer to the One Prayed to than the one who is passing by in front of him, but that is for etiquette of the Salāt and its reverence’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ‘Uthman ibn ‘Isa from ibn Muskan from ibn abu Ya‘fur who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man whose Salah (prayer) is discontinued because of something moving in front of him. He (the Imam) said, ‘Things do not discontinue Salah (prayer) of the believer, but guard it as much as you can.’”

“In the narration of ibn Muskan from abu Basir from abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, it is said that things do not discontinue Salah (prayer), not a dog, donkey and woman, but place a barrier in front of yourselves, of the size of one yard high above ground; it is enough of a barrier.’”

Al-Kulayni has said that it is better to establish a barrier with something, which you can place in front of yourselves and those passing-by. If you did not do so, it is not harmful because the one for whom one performs Salah (prayer) is closer than passing-by one, but it is a matter of the discipline of Salah (prayer) and its respect.
